--- packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/document.go	
+++ packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/document.go	
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+package did
+
+import "time"
+
+type DIDDocument struct {
+	Context            []string             `json:"@context"`
+	ID                 string               `json:"id"`
+	VerificationMethod []VerificationMethod `json:"verificationMethod"`
+	Authentication     []string             `json:"authentication"`
+	AssertionMethod    []string             `json:"assertionMethod"`
+	Created            time.Time            `json:"created"`
+	Updated            time.Time            `json:"updated"`
+}
+
+type VerificationMethod struct {
+	ID                 string `json:"id"`
+	Type               string `json:"type"`
+	Controller         string `json:"controller"`
+	PublicKeyMultibase string `json:"publicKeyMultibase"`
+}

Index: packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/routes/did.go
===================================================================
--- packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/routes/did.go	
+++ packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/routes/did.go	
@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+package routes
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/knirvcorp/knirvoracle/internal/oracle/did"
+)
+
+func (r *OracleRoutes) handleDIDRegister(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
+	if req.Method != http.MethodPost {
+		http.Error(w, "Method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
+		return
+	}
+
+	var doc did.DIDDocument
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(req.Body).Decode(&doc); err != nil {
+		http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("Invalid request: %v", err), http.StatusBadRequest)
+		return
+	}
+
+	resolver := r.oracle.GetDIDResolver()
+	if err := resolver.Register(&doc); err != nil {
+		http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("Registration failed: %v", err), http.StatusBadRequest)
+		return
+	}
+
+	respondJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, doc)
+}
+
+func (r *OracleRoutes) handleDIDResolve(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
+	if req.Method != http.MethodGet {
+		http.Error(w, "Method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
+		return
+	}
+
+	didStr := strings.TrimPrefix(req.URL.Path, "/oracle/v3/did/")
+	if didStr == "" {
+		http.Error(w, "DID is required", http.StatusBadRequest)
+		return
+	}
+
+	resolver := r.oracle.GetDIDResolver()
+	doc, err := resolver.Resolve(didStr)
+	if err != nil {
+		http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("Resolution failed: %v", err), http.StatusNotFound)
+		return
+	}
+
+	respondJSON(w, http.StatusOK, doc)
+}
+
+func (r *OracleRoutes) handleDIDDeactivate(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
+	if req.Method != http.MethodPost {
+		http.Error(w, "Method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
+		return
+	}
+
+	didStr := strings.TrimPrefix(req.URL.Path, "/oracle/v3/did/")
+	didStr = strings.TrimSuffix(didStr, "/deactivate")
+
+	if didStr == "" {
+		http.Error(w, "DID is required", http.StatusBadRequest)
+		return
+	}
+
+	resolver := r.oracle.GetDIDResolver()
+	if err := resolver.Deactivate(didStr); err != nil {
+		http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("Deactivation failed: %v", err), http.StatusBadRequest)
+		return
+	}
+
+	respondJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]interface{}{
+		"status":    "deactivated",
+		"deactivated_at": time.Now().UTC(),
+	})
+}
+
+func (r *OracleRoutes) RegisterDIDRoutes(mux *http.ServeMux) {
+	mux.HandleFunc("/oracle/v3/did/register", r.handleDIDRegister)
+	mux.HandleFunc("/oracle/v3/did/", r.handleDIDResolve)
+	mux.HandleFunc("/oracle/v3/did/", r.handleDIDDeactivate)
+}

Index: packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/identitybridge/revocation.go
===================================================================
--- packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/identitybridge/revocation.go	
+++ packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/identitybridge/revocation.go	
@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+package identitybridge
+
+import (
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"encoding/hex"
+	"fmt"
+	"sync"
+	"time"
+)
+
+type RevocationEntry struct {
+	IdentityID string    `json:"identity_id"`
+	NodeID     string    `json:"node_id"`
+	Reason     string    `json:"reason"`
+	RevokedAt  time.Time `json:"revoked_at"`
+	RevokedBy  string    `json:"revoked_by"`
+	ChainHash  string    `json:"chain_hash"`
+}
+
+type RevocationList struct {
+	mu      sync.RWMutex
+	entries []*RevocationEntry
+	index   map[string]int
+	tip     string
+}
+
+func NewRevocationList() *RevocationList {
+	return &RevocationList{
+		entries: make([]*RevocationEntry, 0),
+		index:   make(map[string]int),
+	}
+}
+
+func (rl *RevocationList) Revoke(identityID, nodeID, reason, revokedBy string) *RevocationEntry {
+	rl.mu.Lock()
+	defer rl.mu.Unlock()
+
+	entry := &RevocationEntry{
+		IdentityID: identityID,
+		NodeID:     nodeID,
+		Reason:     reason,
+		RevokedAt:  time.Now().UTC(),
+		RevokedBy:  revokedBy,
+	}
+
+	chainInput := rl.tip + entry.IdentityID + entry.NodeID + entry.Reason + entry.RevokedBy + entry.RevokedAt.String()
+	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(chainInput))
+	entry.ChainHash = hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
+	rl.tip = entry.ChainHash
+
+	rl.index[identityID] = len(rl.entries)
+	rl.entries = append(rl.entries, entry)
+
+	return entry
+}
+
+func (rl *RevocationList) IsRevoked(identityID string) bool {
+	rl.mu.RLock()
+	defer rl.mu.RUnlock()
+	_, ok := rl.index[identityID]
+	return ok
+}
+
+func (rl *RevocationList) VerifyChain() error {
+	rl.mu.RLock()
+	defer rl.mu.RUnlock()
+
+	if len(rl.entries) == 0 {
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	var prevHash string
+	for i, entry := range rl.entries {
+		chainInput := prevHash + entry.IdentityID + entry.NodeID + entry.Reason + entry.RevokedBy + entry.RevokedAt.String()
+		hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(chainInput))
+		computedHash := hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
+
+		if computedHash != entry.ChainHash {
+			return fmt.Errorf("chain integrity violated at entry %d: expected hash %s, got %s", i, entry.ChainHash, computedHash)
+		}
+		prevHash = entry.ChainHash
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (rl *RevocationList) Export() []*RevocationEntry {
+	rl.mu.RLock()
+	defer rl.mu.RUnlock()
+
+	result := make([]*RevocationEntry, len(rl.entries))
+	copy(result, rl.entries)
+	return result
+}
+
+func (rl *RevocationList) Len() int {
+	rl.mu.RLock()
+	defer rl.mu.RUnlock()
+	return len(rl.entries)
+}
+
+func (rl *RevocationList) TipHash() string {
+	rl.mu.RLock()
+	defer rl.mu.RUnlock()
+	return rl.tip
+}

1: # KNIRVSERVER Governance Implementation Plan
2: 
3: **Reference:** `governanceToolkitComparison.html` — AGT gap analysis  
4: **Scope:** Native Go implementations only. No Python FFI, no AGT library imports.  
5: **Baseline:** Phases 1–4 scaffolding is live (`identitybridge`, `policyadapter`, `reliability`, `mcphardening` + `governance_handlers.go` routes).
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Current State Summary
10: 
11: All four roadmap phases from the comparison document have been scaffolded as Go packages wired into the KNIRVSERVER HTTP layer:
12: 
13: | Phase | Package | Route prefix | Status |
14: |-------|---------|--------------|--------|
15: | 1 — Identity bridge | `services/identitybridge` | `/api/v1/governance/identity` | Scaffolded |
16: | 2 — Policy adapter | `services/policyadapter` | `/api/v1/governance/policy` | Scaffolded |
17: | 3 — Reliability controls | `services/reliability` | `/api/v1/governance/reliability` | Scaffolded |
18: | 4 — MCP hardening | `services/mcphardening` | `/api/v1/governance/mcp` | Scaffolded |
19: 
20: The scaffolding covers struct definitions, basic CRUD, and in-memory state. What is missing is the functional depth that makes these layers governance-grade: policy evaluation, DID resolution, zero-trust continuous verification, compliance evidence generation, framework interoperability, and a verification CLI.
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## Gap Analysis by Layer
25: 
26: ### Layer 1: Identity Bridge
27: 
28: **Implemented:** `TrustEnvelope` creation/expiry/revocation, trust score arithmetic, `TrustMapping` for external source aliasing, federation flag, HTTP handlers.
29: 
30: **Missing:**
31: 
32: | Gap | Why it matters |
33: |-----|---------------|
34: | DID document resolution | `IdentitySourceDID` is a string constant; no W3C DID resolution happens |
35: | Zero-trust middleware | Envelopes are only checked on explicit API call, not per-request |
36: | OIDC/X509 parsing | `IdentitySourceOIDC`/`IdentitySourceX509` are declared but inert |
37: | Hard revocation log | `RevokeEnvelope` soft-expires; nothing external can query a revocation list |
38: | Continuous trust decay | Trust scores are set once and drift upward via delta; no time-based decay |
39: 
40: ### Layer 2: Policy Adapter
41: 
42: **Implemented:** `NormalizedPolicyInput` schema, `PolicyEvaluation`/`NormalizedEnforcement` structs, `PortabilityContract` descriptor, `PolicySourceOPA` constant.
43: 
44: **Missing:**
45: 
46: | Gap | Why it matters |
47: |-----|---------------|
48: | Embedded Rego evaluator | `PolicySourceOPA` is a constant with no evaluation path |
49: | Policy-as-code DSL | Currently stores normalized inputs; no rule evaluation occurs |
50: | Per-request enforcement middleware | `NormalizeInput` is called manually; it doesn't intercept real requests |
51: | Hot-reload without restart | No file-watch or gRPC trigger to push new rules at runtime |
52: | GuardrailEngine integration | `policyadapter` and `guardrails` service are completely separate; no bridge |
53: 
54: ### Layer 3: Reliability Controls
55: 
56: **Implemented:** `CircuitBreaker` (closed/open/half-open), `ErrorBudget`, `KillSwitch` arm/trip, `BreachEvent` log, statistics.
57: 
58: **Missing:**
59: 
60: | Gap | Why it matters |
61: |-----|---------------|
62: | DVE metric binding | Breakers track synthetic test calls; they are not wired to real DVE CPU/memory/latency |
63: | Escalation notification | When a kill switch fires, no other service is notified |
64: | SLO/SLA definitions | There is no concept of target reliability level or window |
65: | GuardrailEngine bridge | `ValidateResourceUsage` in guardrails is disconnected from `ReliabilityController` |
66: | Breach persistence | `breachEvents` are in-memory; crash loses history |
67: 
68: ### Layer 4: MCP Hardening
69: 
70: **Implemented:** `ToolDefinition` registry, `PoisoningSignature` pattern matching, `ToolCallRecord` audit log, `MCPEndpoint` config, gateway statistics.
71: 
72: **Missing:**
73: 
74: | Gap | Why it matters |
75: |-----|---------------|
76: | Argument schema validation | Poisoning detection checks tool name patterns, not call argument content |
77: | Prompt injection detection | No analysis of string arguments for injection payloads |
78: | Response-side audit | Only call records exist; tool responses are not captured |
79: | KNIRVGATEWAY integration | MCP gateway sits in KNIRVSERVER but doesn't intercept KNIRVGATEWAY-routed MCP calls |
80: | Tool capability binding | No link from `ToolDefinition` to KNIRVCHAIN `CapabilityNode` records |
81: 
82: ### Layer 5: Compliance / Verification (entirely missing)
83: 
84: AGT ships an `agent-governance-toolkit-cli` with a `verify` subcommand that produces cryptographically-bound compliance reports. KNIRVSERVER has `fintech/evidence_pack.go` but no cross-service compliance layer.
85: 
86: **Missing:**
87: 
88: - Compliance framework mapping (GDPR Article 22, SOC 2 CC6, ISO 42001 controls) over real KNIRVSERVER events
89: - Cross-service evidence correlator that joins identity + policy + reliability + MCP audit records into a single report
90: - HMAC chain over the audit log so evidence cannot be retroactively altered
91: - `knirvctl governance verify` CLI subcommand
92: 
93: ### Layer 6: Framework Interoperability (partially missing)
94: 
95: AGT differentiates on adapter coverage (LangChain, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, etc.). KNIRVSERVER exposes REST. What's missing is a governance middleware SDK that external Go-based runtimes can embed without making REST calls.
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## Implementation Plan
100: 
101: ### Phase 1-A: DID Resolution Engine
102: 
103: DID resolution belongs entirely in **KNIRVORACLE** (`packages/KNIRVORACLE/`, module `github.com/knirvcorp/knirvoracle`), which is the authoritative trust and identity service in the KNIRV network. KNIRVSERVER's `identitybridge` does not implement its own resolver — it calls KNIRVORACLE's HTTP API (`:1317`) when `IdentitySourceDID` is specified.
104: 
105: #### 1-A-i: Resolver implementation in KNIRVORACLE
106: 
107: **New files:**
108: 
109: - `packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/resolver.go` — core resolver logic
110: - `packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/document.go` — DID document types
111: - `packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/routes/did.go` — HTTP handler wired into the existing routes in `routes/routes.go`
112: 
113: The resolver uses KNIRVORACLE's existing `internal/oracle/crypto/` package (already has `ecdsa.go`, `address.go`, `keccak.go`) and adds Ed25519 support alongside it:
114: 
115: ```go
116: // packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/document.go
117: package did
118: 
119: type DIDDocument struct {
120:     Context            []string             `json:"@context"`
121:     ID                 string               `json:"id"`
122:     VerificationMethod []VerificationMethod `json:"verificationMethod"`
123:     Authentication     []string             `json:"authentication"`
124:     AssertionMethod    []string             `json:"assertionMethod"`
125:     Created            time.Time            `json:"created"`
126:     Updated            time.Time            `json:"updated"`
127: }
128: 
129: type VerificationMethod struct {
130:     ID                 string `json:"id"`
131:     Type               string `json:"type"`               // Ed25519VerificationKey2020
132:     Controller         string `json:"controller"`
133:     PublicKeyMultibase string `json:"publicKeyMultibase"` // multibase-encoded Ed25519 pubkey
134: }
135: ```
136: 
137: ```go
138: // packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/resolver.go
139: package did
140: 
141: type Method string
142: 
143: const (
144:     MethodKNIRV Method = "knirv" // did:knirv:<nodeID> — stored in oracle ledger
145:     MethodKey   Method = "key"   // did:key:<multibase-pubkey> — resolved locally
146: )
147: 
148: type Resolver struct {
149:     store DIDStore // interface over oracle's internal ledger
150: }
151: 
152: type DIDStore interface {
153:     Get(did string) (*DIDDocument, error)
154:     Put(doc *DIDDocument) error
155:     Deactivate(did string) error
156: }
157: 
158: func NewResolver(store DIDStore) *Resolver
159: func (r *Resolver) Resolve(did string) (*DIDDocument, error)    // dispatches by method
160: func (r *Resolver) Register(doc *DIDDocument) error
161: func (r *Resolver) Deactivate(did string) error
162: func (r *Resolver) resolveKNIRV(id string) (*DIDDocument, error) // ledger lookup
163: func (r *Resolver) resolveKey(encoded string) (*DIDDocument, error) // local Ed25519 decode
164: ```
165: 
166: `did:key:` resolution decodes the multibase-encoded Ed25519 public key inline using `golang.org/x/crypto/ed25519` — no network call. `did:knirv:` documents are stored in KNIRVORACLE's own ledger (not KNIRVCHAIN), keyed by node ID, and written when a node first registers with the oracle.
167: 
168: **New HTTP routes added to `packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/routes/did.go`** and registered in `routes/routes.go`:
169: 
170: ```
171: POST /did/register     — register a new did:knirv: document
172: GET  /did/{did}        — resolve any supported DID (did:knirv: or did:key:)
173: POST /did/{did}/deactivate — deactivate a did:knirv: document
174: ```
175: 
176: These sit at the same `:1317` port as all other KNIRVORACLE routes.
177: 
178: #### 1-A-ii: KNIRVSERVER identity bridge integration
179: 
180: `identitybridge/service.go` does not get a `did.go` file. Instead, when `IdentitySourceDID` is specified in `CreateEnvelope`, the bridge makes a single HTTP GET to KNIRVORACLE:
181: 
182: ```
183: GET http://localhost:1317/did/{did}
184: ```
185: 
186: It parses the returned `DIDDocument`, extracts the `Ed25519VerificationKey2020` verification method, verifies the envelope request's signature against that key, and if valid produces the `TrustEnvelope`. The oracle URL is read from config (`governance.did.oracle_url`, defaulting to `http://localhost:1317`).
187: 
188: This keeps KNIRVSERVER free of any DID ledger responsibility and respects the existing boundary: KNIRVORACLE is the root of trust, KNIRVSERVER enforces downstream.
189: 
190: ---
191: 
192: ### Phase 1-B: Zero-Trust Per-Request Middleware
193: 
194: **File:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/web/middleware/governance.go`
195: 
196: This lives in the existing `middleware` package alongside `auth.go`, `middleware.go`, and `pwa.go`. It follows the same struct-with-constructor pattern as `AuthMiddleware` and returns `func(http.Handler) http.Handler` (the Gorilla Mux HTTP handler form — matching `CORSMiddlewareHTTP` in the same package).
197: 
198: **Integration with `AuthMiddleware`:** The governance middleware runs *after* JWT auth in the middleware chain. It reads the `AuthContext` already stored at `AuthContextKey` by `AuthMiddleware`, so it does not re-validate the JWT. Instead it reads the `X-KNIRV-Identity` header (a `TrustEnvelope.IdentityID`) and performs the governance trust check using the identity already authenticated:
199: 
200: ```
201: CORSMiddlewareHTTP() → AuthMiddleware.Require() → GovernanceMiddleware.Enforce() → handler
202: ```
203: 
204: The middleware:
205: 
206: 1. Reads `AuthContextKey` from the request context (set by `AuthMiddleware`) — returns 401 if absent (auth must precede governance).
207: 2. Reads `X-KNIRV-Identity` header for the `TrustEnvelope.IdentityID`.
208: 3. Looks up the envelope from `IdentityBridge` and checks `RevocationList.IsRevoked`.
209: 4. Checks expiry and minimum trust level for the route's tier.
210: 5. Applies a time-based trust decay (`TrustDecayRate` config — e.g. 0.001 per hour since `IssuedAt`).
211: 6. If trust falls below threshold, returns HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: KNIRV-Identity`.
212: 7. Stores the resolved `TrustEnvelope` in the request context under its own `contextKey` for downstream handlers.
213: 
214: ```go
215: package middleware
216: 
217: // GovernanceTrustKey is the context key for the resolved TrustEnvelope.
218: const GovernanceTrustKey contextKey = "governance_trust"
219: 
220: type GovernanceMiddleware struct {
221:     bridge    *identitybridge.IdentityBridge
222:     revoked   *identitybridge.RevocationList
223:     tiered    map[string]identitybridge.TrustLevel // route prefix → minimum level
224:     decayRate float64
225: }
226: 
227: func NewGovernanceMiddleware(
228:     bridge *identitybridge.IdentityBridge,
229:     revoked *identitybridge.RevocationList,
230:     tiers map[string]identitybridge.TrustLevel,
231:     decayRate float64,
232: ) *GovernanceMiddleware
233: 
234: func (gm *GovernanceMiddleware) Enforce(next http.Handler) http.Handler
235: func GovernanceTrustFromContext(ctx context.Context) *identitybridge.TrustEnvelope
236: ```
237: 
238: `GovernanceTrustFromContext` is the public accessor downstream handlers use, mirroring `GetRequestID` in `middleware.go`.
239: 
240: Route tier table (configured in `config/governance.yaml`):
241: 
242: ```yaml
243: governance:
244:   zero_trust:
245:     tiers:
246:       "/api/v1/governance/identity": high
247:       "/api/v1/governance/policy":   medium
248:       "/api/v1/governance/reliability": high
249:       "/api/v1/governance/mcp":      high
250:       "/oracle/":                    maximum
251:     decay_rate_per_hour: 0.001
252: ```
253: 
254: ---
255: 
256: ### Phase 1-C: Hard Revocation List
257: 
258: **File:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/identitybridge/revocation.go`
259: 
260: A concurrent-safe revocation list with a tamper-evident append-only log:
261: 
262: ```go
263: type RevocationEntry struct {
264:     IdentityID string    `json:"identity_id"`
265:     NodeID     string    `json:"node_id"`
266:     Reason     string    `json:"reason"`
267:     RevokedAt  time.Time `json:"revoked_at"`
268:     RevokedBy  string    `json:"revoked_by"`
269:     ChainHash  string    `json:"chain_hash"` // SHA-256 of previous entry + this entry
270: }
271: 
272: type RevocationList struct {
273:     mu      sync.RWMutex
274:     entries []*RevocationEntry
275:     index   map[string]int // identityID → slice position
276:     tip     string         // hash of last entry
277: }
278: 
279: func (rl *RevocationList) Revoke(identityID, nodeID, reason, revokedBy string) *RevocationEntry
280: func (rl *RevocationList) IsRevoked(identityID string) bool
281: func (rl *RevocationList) VerifyChain() error  // recomputes all hashes
282: func (rl *RevocationList) Export() []*RevocationEntry
283: ```
284: 
285: `IdentityBridge.GetEnvelope` checks `RevocationList.IsRevoked` before returning a valid envelope.
286: 
287: **New HTTP routes:**
288: - `GET /api/v1/governance/identity/revocation` — export full list
289: - `GET /api/v1/governance/identity/revocation/verify` — verify chain integrity
290: 
291: ---
292: 
293: ### Phase 2-A: Embedded Rego Evaluator
294: 
295: **File:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/policyadapter/rego.go`
296: 
297: Embed a Rego policy evaluator using `github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/rego` (pure Go, no cgo). This keeps enforcement inside KNIRVSERVER without shelling out or calling an external OPA server.
298: 
299: ```go
300: type RegoEvaluator struct {
301:     mu       sync.RWMutex
302:     modules  map[string]string // policyID → Rego source
303:     prepared map[string]*rego.PreparedEvalQuery
304: }
305: 
306: func NewRegoEvaluator() *RegoEvaluator
307: func (re *RegoEvaluator) LoadPolicy(policyID, regoSource string) error
308: func (re *RegoEvaluator) UnloadPolicy(policyID string) error
309: func (re *RegoEvaluator) Evaluate(policyID string, input map[string]interface{}) (*PolicyEvaluation, error)
310: func (re *RegoEvaluator) HotReload(policyID, newSource string) error  // atomic swap
311: ```
312:

327: ### Phase 2-B: Per-Request Policy Enforcement Middleware
328: 
329: **File:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/web/middleware/governance.go` (same file as Phase 1-B)
330: 
331: Extend `GovernanceMiddleware` to accept a `*policyadapter.PolicyAdapter` and `*policyadapter.RegoEvaluator` at construction. After the identity check passes, `Enforce` calls `PolicyAdapter.NormalizeInput` using the request's action type (derived from HTTP method + route prefix) and then `RegoEvaluator.Evaluate`. The `TrustEnvelope` resolved in the identity step is injected as a context field in the policy input, so Rego rules can condition on trust level directly.
332: 
333: If the policy decision is `deny`, the middleware returns HTTP 403 with the matched rules serialized in the body. No further handler invocation occurs.
334: 
335: The full enforcement chain through the existing middleware stack becomes:
336: 
337: ```
338: CORSMiddlewareHTTP()
339:   → RequestIDMiddleware()     [middleware.go — adds X-Request-ID]
340:   → AuthMiddleware.Require()  [auth.go — validates JWT, stores AuthContext]
341:   → GovernanceMiddleware.Enforce()  [governance.go — trust check → policy eval]
342:       → handler
343: ```
344: 
345: On denial at any governance step:
346: ```
347: identity expired/revoked  → 401  WWW-Authenticate: KNIRV-Identity
348: trust below tier minimum  → 401  WWW-Authenticate: KNIRV-Identity
349: policy decision = deny    → 403  {matched_rules: [...]}
350: ```

522: ### Phase 4-B: Prompt Injection Detection
523: 
524: **File:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/mcphardening/injection.go`
525: 
526: A pure-Go string-argument scanner for prompt injection patterns, run after schema validation:
527: 
528: ```go
529: type InjectionSignature struct {
530:     Pattern     string  // compiled regexp
531:     Weight      float64 // 0..1
532:     Description string
533: }
534: 
535: type InjectionDetector struct {
536:     mu         sync.RWMutex
537:     signatures []*compiledInjectionSig  // pre-compiled *regexp.Regexp
538:     threshold  float64
539: }
540: 
541: type InjectionResult struct {
542:     Score      float64
543:     Triggered  []string  // matched signature descriptions
544:     Blocked    bool
545: }
546: 
547: func NewInjectionDetector(threshold float64) *InjectionDetector
548: func (id *InjectionDetector) RegisterSignature(sig InjectionSignature) error
549: func (id *InjectionDetector) Scan(args map[string]interface{}) InjectionResult
550: ```
551: 
552: Default signatures loaded at startup cover common injection patterns:
553: - `ignore previous instructions`
554: - `system prompt override`
555: - `<|im_start|>system` / `<|im_end|>` token boundaries
556: - Unicode lookalike character sequences in argument keys
557: - Recursive self-reference chains (`tool calls tool calls tool`)

559: `InjectionDetector` is added to `MCPGateway`. `ProcessToolCall` runs `InjectionDetector.Scan` over all string-typed arguments after schema validation.

591: ### Phase 5: Compliance Evidence Layer (new package)
592: 
593: **Package:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/compliance`
594: 
595: This is the missing layer that AGT's `agent-governance-toolkit-sre` and verification CLI provide. It correlates events from all four governance services into framework-mapped compliance reports.
596: 
597: #### 5-A: Event Correlator
598: 
599: **File:** `services/compliance/correlator.go`
600: 
601: ```go
602: type ComplianceEvent struct {
603:     ID        string            `json:"id"`
604:     Timestamp time.Time         `json:"timestamp"`
605:     Source    string            `json:"source"`  // identity | policy | reliability | mcp
606:     EventType string            `json:"event_type"`
607:     EntityID  string            `json:"entity_id"`
608:     NodeID    string            `json:"node_id"`
609:     AgentID   string            `json:"agent_id,omitempty"`
610:     Outcome   string            `json:"outcome"` // allow | deny | flag | breach | kill
611:     Detail    map[string]interface{} `json:"detail"`
612:     ChainHash string            `json:"chain_hash"`
613: }
614: 
615: type EventCorrelator struct {
616:     mu     sync.RWMutex
617:     events []*ComplianceEvent
618:     tip    string  // running HMAC-SHA256 chain tip
619:     key    []byte  // HMAC key loaded from root.key
620: }
621: 
622: func (ec *EventCorrelator) Record(source, eventType, entityID, nodeID, agentID, outcome string, detail map[string]interface{})
623: func (ec *EventCorrelator) VerifyChain() error
624: func (ec *EventCorrelator) Query(filter EventFilter) []*ComplianceEvent
625: func (ec *EventCorrelator) Export(format string) ([]byte, error)  // json | csv | ndjson
626: ```

628: Each governance service receives an `*EventCorrelator` at construction and calls `correlator.Record` on every meaningful state change. The HMAC chain makes each event cryptographically dependent on the previous one — retroactive alteration requires the HMAC key.

630: The HMAC key is derived from KNIRVSERVER's existing `root.key` secret store.

690: **Files:**
691: 
692: | File | Role |
693: |------|------|
694: | `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance.go` | Declares `governanceCmd`, registers it on `rootCmd` in `init()`, adds subcommand group |
695: | `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance/verify.go` | `VerifyCmd` — verify HMAC chain |
696: | `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance/report.go` | `ReportCmd` — generate compliance report |

702: 
703: ```go
704: package cmd
705: 
706: import (
707:     "github.com/KNIRV/KNIRV_NETWORK/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance"
708:     "github.com/spf13/cobra"
709: )
710: 
711: var governanceCmd = &cobra.Command{
712:     Use:   "governance",
713:     Short: "Inspect and verify KNIRVSERVER governance state",
714:     Long:  `Query trust envelopes, policy decisions, compliance evidence, and MCP audit records from a running KNIRVSERVER instance.`,
715:     Run:   func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) { cmd.Help() },
716: }

719:     rootCmd.AddCommand(governanceCmd)
720:     governanceCmd.AddCommand(governance.VerifyCmd)

728: **Conventions (match existing KNIRVSHELL cmd style):**
729: 
730: - Use `github.com/spf13/cobra` for all commands (not `flag`).
731: - Use the package-level `log` (`logrus.New()` from `root.go`) for output — do not create a second logger.
732: - Use `viper.GetString("node_url")` to read `--node-url` from the inherited persistent flag rather than defining a new flag.
733: - HTTP calls go to `viper.GetString("node_url")` (default `http://localhost:8084`). Auth token is read from `~/.knirv.yaml` via viper key `governance.token`.

748: ### Phase 7: Framework Interoperability SDK
749: 
750: The SDK is split across two packages matching the existing project split between KNIRVBASE (importable library) and KNIRVSERVER (the running process):
751: 
752: #### 7-A: Client — `packages/KNIRVSDK/go/governance/`
753: 
754: **Module:** `github.com/KNIRV/KNIRV_NETWORK/KNIRVSDK/go` (declared in `packages/KNIRVSDK/go/go.mod`)
755: 
756: **New package path within module:** `github.com/KNIRV/KNIRV_NETWORK/KNIRVSDK/go/governance`
757: 
758: This sits alongside the existing SDK subdirectories — `gateway/`, `transaction/`, `transmission/`, `oracled/` — following the same flat layout. External agent frameworks import this package to embed governance checks without making HTTP calls. It communicates with the `GovernanceAgent` server (Phase 7-B) over a Unix domain socket, keeping the enforcement path sub-millisecond.
759: 
760: No new entries in `packages/KNIRVSDK/go/go.mod` are required — the socket client only needs `net`, `encoding/json`, and `sync` from the standard library.
761: 
762: ```go
763: // packages/KNIRVSDK/go/governance/client.go
764: package governance
765: 
766: // Types are declared locally so KNIRVSDK has no dependency on KNIRVSERVER internals.
767: type TrustEnvelope struct {
768:     IdentityID string     `json:"identity_id"`
769:     NodeID     string     `json:"node_id"`
770:     AgentID    string     `json:"agent_id,omitempty"`
771:     TrustLevel string     `json:"trust_level"`
772:     TrustScore float64    `json:"trust_score"`
773:     ExpiresAt  time.Time  `json:"expires_at"`
774: }
775: 
776: type PolicyInput struct {
777:     NodeID     string                 `json:"node_id"`
778:     AgentID    string                 `json:"agent_id,omitempty"`
779:     Action     string                 `json:"action"`
780:     ActionType string                 `json:"action_type"`
781:     Metrics    map[string]float64     `json:"metrics,omitempty"`
782:     Context    map[string]interface{} `json:"context,omitempty"`
783: }
784: 
785: type PolicyDecision struct {
786:     Decision     string   `json:"decision"`      // allow | deny
787:     Reason       string   `json:"reason,omitempty"`
788:     MatchedRules []string `json:"matched_rules,omitempty"`
789: }
790: 
791: type ToolCallStatus string
792: 
793: const (
794:     ToolCallAllowed  ToolCallStatus = "allowed"
795:     ToolCallDenied   ToolCallStatus = "denied"
796:     ToolCallFlagged  ToolCallStatus = "flagged"
797:     ToolCallBlocked  ToolCallStatus = "blocked"
798: )
799: 
800: // DefaultSocketPath is exported so the KNIRVSERVER GovernanceAgent and this
801: // client agree on the socket location without requiring config on both sides.
802: const DefaultSocketPath = "/var/run/knirvserver/governance.sock"
803: 
804: type Client struct {
805:     socketPath string
806:     conn       net.Conn
807:     mu         sync.Mutex
808: }
809: 
810: func NewClient(socketPath string) (*Client, error)
811: func (c *Client) CheckIdentity(nodeID, agentID string) (*TrustEnvelope, error)
812: func (c *Client) EvaluatePolicy(input PolicyInput) (*PolicyDecision, error)
813: func (c *Client) RecordToolCall(agentID, nodeID, toolName string, args map[string]interface{}) (ToolCallStatus, error)
814: func (c *Client) Close() error
815: ```
816: 
817: The socket protocol — length-prefixed JSON (4-byte big-endian length + JSON body) — is the full wire contract. Any language can implement a compatible client without a generated stub.
818:

820: 
821: Runs as a goroutine inside the main KNIRVSERVER process, started during server initialization alongside the other governance services. Uses the same socket path constant (`governance.DefaultSocketPath` or the override from `governance.sdk.socket_path` in `config/governance.yaml`).

823: ```go

825: package governance_sdk
826: 
827: type GovernanceAgent struct {
828:     socketPath string
829:     identity   *identitybridge.IdentityBridge
830:     policy     *policyadapter.PolicyAdapter
831:     mcp        *mcphardening.MCPGateway
832:     listener   net.Listener

837:     ib  *identitybridge.IdentityBridge,
838:     pa  *policyadapter.PolicyAdapter,
839:     mcp *mcphardening.MCPGateway,

842: func (ga *GovernanceAgent) Start() error  // spawns accept loop goroutine

850: ## Sequencing and Dependencies
851: 
852: ```
853: 1-A DID resolver          → 1-B zero-trust middleware (needs envelope validation)
854: 1-C revocation list       → 1-B (needs IsRevoked check)
855: 2-A Rego evaluator        → 2-B per-request enforcement (needs evaluator)

101: ### Phase 1-A: DID Resolution Engine
102: 
103: DID resolution belongs entirely in **KNIRVORACLE** (`packages/KNIRVORACLE/`, module `github.com/knirvcorp/knirvoracle`), which is the authoritative trust and identity service in the KNIRV network. KNIRVSERVER's `identitybridge` does not implement its own resolver — it calls KNIRVORACLE's HTTP API (`:1317`) when `IdentitySourceDID` is specified.
104: 
105: #### 1-A-i: Resolver implementation in KNIRVORACLE
106: 
107: **New files:**
108: 
109: - `packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/resolver.go` — core resolver logic
110: - `packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/document.go` — DID document types
111: - `packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/routes/did.go` — HTTP handler wired into the existing routes in `routes/routes.go`
112: 
113: The resolver uses KNIRVORACLE's existing `internal/oracle/crypto/` package (already has `ecdsa.go`, `address.go`, `keccak.go`) and adds Ed25519 support alongside it:
114: 
115: ```go
116: // packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/document.go
117: package did
118: 
119: type DIDDocument struct {
120:     Context            []string             `json:"@context"`
121:     ID                 string               `json:"id"`
122:     VerificationMethod []VerificationMethod `json:"verificationMethod"`
123:     Authentication     []string             `json:"authentication"`
124:     AssertionMethod    []string             `json:"assertionMethod"`
125:     Created            time.Time            `json:"created"`
126:     Updated            time.Time            `json:"updated"`
127: }
128: 
129: type VerificationMethod struct {
130:     ID                 string `json:"id"`
131:     Type               string `json:"type"`               // Ed25519VerificationKey2020
132:     Controller         string `json:"controller"`
133:     PublicKeyMultibase string `json:"publicKeyMultibase"` // multibase-encoded Ed25519 pubkey
134: }
135: ```
136: 
137: ```go
138: // packages/KNIRVORACLE/internal/oracle/did/resolver.go
139: package did
140: 
141: type Method string
142: 
143: const (
144:     MethodKNIRV Method = "knirv" // did:knirv:<nodeID> — stored in oracle ledger
145:     MethodKey   Method = "key"   // did:key:<multibase-pubkey> — resolved locally
146: )
147: 
148: type Resolver struct {
149:     store DIDStore // interface over oracle's internal ledger
150: }
151: 
152: type DIDStore interface {
153:     Get(did string) (*DIDDocument, error)
154:     Put(doc *DIDDocument) error
155:     Deactivate(did string) error
156: }
157: 
158: func NewResolver(store DIDStore) *Resolver
159: func (r *Resolver) Resolve(did string) (*DIDDocument, error)    // dispatches by method
160: func (r *Resolver) Register(doc *DIDDocument) error
161: func (r *Resolver) Deactivate(did string) error
162: func (r *Resolver) resolveKNIRV(id string) (*DIDDocument, error) // ledger lookup
163: func (r *Resolver) resolveKey(encoded string) (*DIDDocument, error) // local Ed25519 decode
164: ```

166: `did:key:` resolution decodes the multibase-encoded Ed25519 public key inline using `golang.org/x/crypto/ed25519` — no network call. `did:knirv:` documents are stored in KNIRVORACLE's own ledger (not KNIRVCHAIN), keyed by node ID, and written when a node first registers with the oracle.

172: GET  /did/{did}        — resolve any supported DID (did:knirv: or did:key:)
173: POST /did/{did}/deactivate — deactivate a did:knirv: document
174: ```

176: These sit at the same `:1317` port as all other KNIRVORACLE routes.

179: 
180: `identitybridge/service.go` does not get a `did.go` file. Instead, when `IdentitySourceDID` is specified in `CreateEnvelope`, the bridge makes a single HTTP GET to KNIRVORACLE:

The oracle URL is read from config (`governance.did.oracle_url`, defaulting to `http://localhost:1317`).

192: ### Phase 1-B: Zero-Trust Per-Request Middleware
193: 
194: **File:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/web/middleware/governance.go`
195: 
196: This lives in the existing `middleware` package alongside `auth.go`, `middleware.go`, and `pwa.go`. It follows the same struct-with-constructor pattern as `AuthMiddleware` and returns `func(http.Handler) http.Handler` (the Gorilla Mux HTTP handler form — matching `CORSMiddlewareHTTP` in the same package).
197: 
198: **Integration with `AuthMiddleware`:** The governance middleware runs *after* JWT auth in the middleware chain. It reads the `AuthContext` already stored at `AuthContextKey` by `AuthMiddleware`, so it does not re-validate the JWT. Instead it reads the `X-KNIRV-Identity` header (a `TrustEnvelope.IdentityID`) and performs the governance trust check using the identity already authenticated:
199: 
200: ```
201: CORSMiddlewareHTTP() → AuthMiddleware.Require() → GovernanceMiddleware.Enforce() → handler
202: ```
203: 
204: The middleware:
205: 
206: 1. Reads `AuthContextKey` from the request context (set by `AuthMiddleware`) — returns 401 if absent (auth must precede governance).
207: 2. Reads `X-KNIRV-Identity` header for the `TrustEnvelope.IdentityID`.
208: 3. Looks up the envelope from `IdentityBridge` and checks `RevocationList.IsRevoked`.
209: 4. Checks expiry and minimum trust level for the route's tier.
210: 5. Applies a time-based trust decay (`TrustDecayRate` config — e.g. 0.001 per hour since `IssuedAt`).
211: 6. If trust falls below threshold, returns HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: KNIRV-Identity`.
212: 7. Stores the resolved `TrustEnvelope` in the request context under its own `contextKey` for downstream handlers.
213:

215: package middleware
216: 
217: // GovernanceTrustKey is the context key for the resolved TrustEnvelope.
218: const GovernanceTrustKey contextKey = "governance_trust"
219: 
220: type GovernanceMiddleware struct {
221:     bridge    *identitybridge.IdentityBridge
222:     revoked   *identitybridge.RevocationList
223:     tiered    map[string]identitybridge.TrustLevel // route prefix → minimum level
224:     decayRate float64
225: }
226: 
227: func NewGovernanceMiddleware(
228:     bridge *identitybridge.IdentityBridge,
229:     revoked *identitybridge.RevocationList,
230:     tiers map[string]identitybridge.TrustLevel,
231:     decayRate float64,
232: ) *GovernanceMiddleware
233: 
234: func (gm *GovernanceMiddleware) Enforce(next http.Handler) http.Handler
235: func GovernanceTrustFromContext(ctx context.Context) *identitybridge.TrustEnvelope
236: ```

238: `GovernanceTrustFromContext` is the public accessor downstream handlers use, mirroring `GetRequestID` in `middleware.go`.

370: `ValidateWithGovernance` calls `GuardrailEngine.ValidateResourceUsage`, maps the result into `NormalizeInput`, then calls `RegoEvaluator.Evaluate` if a policy is registered for the resource domain. The `NormalizedEnforcement` is persisted so compliance reports can reference guardrail decisions.

374: ### Phase 3-A: DVE Metric Binding
375: 
376: **File:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/reliability/dve_binding.go`
377: 
378: Connect `ReliabilityController` to the DVE manager so circuit breakers track real node metrics instead of synthetic calls:
379: 
380: ```go
381: type DVEMetricBinding struct {
382:     ctrl       *ReliabilityController
383:     dveManager DVEMetricProvider  // interface over dvemanager.DVEManager
384:     ticker     *time.Ticker
385:     stopCh     chan struct{}
386: }
387: 
388: type DVEMetricProvider interface {
389:     GetNodeMetrics(nodeID string) (cpu, memoryMB, latencyMs float64, err error)
390:     ListActiveNodes() ([]string, error)
391: }
392: 
393: func (b *DVEMetricBinding) Start(interval time.Duration)
394: func (b *DVEMetricBinding) Stop()
395: func (b *DVEMetricBinding) syncOnce()  // called by ticker
396: ```
397: 
398: `syncOnce` iterates all active DVE nodes, reads CPU/memory/latency via `DVEMetricProvider`, and calls the relevant `CircuitBreaker.RecordSuccess` or `RecordFailure` based on threshold config. When a breaker transitions to open, it also calls `ReliabilityController.ArmKillSwitch` for the node.
399: 
400: Thresholds configured in `config/governance.yaml`:
401: 
402: ```yaml
403: governance:
404:   reliability:
405:     dve_binding:
406:       sync_interval: 10s
407:       cpu_threshold: 0.85
408:       memory_threshold_mb: 3072
409:       latency_threshold_ms: 2000
410: ```

414: ### Phase 3-B: Escalation Notification Pipeline
415: 
416: **File:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/reliability/escalation.go`
417: 
418: When a kill switch fires, broadcast the event to registered handlers synchronously before returning:
419: 
420: ```go
421: type EscalationEvent struct {
422:     AgentID   string    `json:"agent_id"`
423:     NodeID    string    `json:"node_id"`
424:     Reason    string    `json:"reason"`
425:     KillAt    time.Time `json:"kill_at"`
426:     Severity  string    `json:"severity"` // warn | critical | fatal
427: }
428: 
429: type EscalationHandler interface {
430:     OnEscalation(event EscalationEvent)
431: }
432: 
433: type EscalationPipeline struct {
434:     mu       sync.RWMutex
435:     handlers []EscalationHandler
436: }
437: 
438: func (ep *EscalationPipeline) Register(h EscalationHandler)
439: func (ep *EscalationPipeline) Fire(event EscalationEvent)
440: ```
441: 
442: Built-in handlers registered at startup:
443: - `WebSocketEscalationHandler` — broadcasts over the existing WebSocket hub (`policy:kill_switch` event type)
444: - `GuardrailEscalationHandler` — calls `GuardrailEngine.BlockNode(nodeID)` immediately
445: - `PolicyEscalationHandler` — records a `NormalizedEnforcement` with decision `block`
446: 
447: `ReliabilityController.TripKillSwitch` gains a `pipeline *EscalationPipeline` field and calls `pipeline.Fire` after updating state.

522: ### Phase 4-B: Prompt Injection Detection
523: 
524: **File:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/mcphardening/injection.go`
525: 
526: A pure-Go string-argument scanner for prompt injection patterns, run after schema validation:
527: 
528: ```go
529: type InjectionSignature struct {
530:     Pattern     string  // compiled regexp
531:     Weight      float64 // 0..1
532:     Description string
533: }
534: 
535: type InjectionDetector struct {
536:     mu         sync.RWMutex
537:     signatures []*compiledInjectionSig  // pre-compiled *regexp.Regexp
538:     threshold  float64
539: }
540: 
541: type InjectionResult struct {
542:     Score      float64
543:     Triggered  []string  // matched signature descriptions
544:     Blocked    bool
545: }
546: 
547: func NewInjectionDetector(threshold float64) *InjectionDetector
548: func (id *InjectionDetector) RegisterSignature(sig InjectionSignature) error
549: func (id *InjectionDetector) Scan(args map[string]interface{}) InjectionResult
550: ```
551: 
552: Default signatures loaded at startup cover common injection patterns:
553: - `ignore previous instructions`
554: - `system prompt override`
555: - `<|im_start|>system` / `<|im_end|>` token boundaries
556: - Unicode lookalike character sequences in argument keys
557: - Recursive self-reference chains (`tool calls tool calls tool`)
558: 
559: `InjectionDetector` is added to `MCPGateway`. `ProcessToolCall` runs `InjectionDetector.Scan` over all string-typed arguments after schema validation.

591: ### Phase 5: Compliance Evidence Layer (new package)
592: 
593: **Package:** `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/compliance`
594: 
595: This is the missing layer that AGT's `agent-governance-toolkit-sre` and verification CLI provide. It correlates events from all four governance services into framework-mapped compliance reports.
596: 
597: #### 5-A: Event Correlator
598: 
599: **File:** `services/compliance/correlator.go`
600: 
601: ```go
602: type ComplianceEvent struct {
603:     ID        string            `json:"id"`
604:     Timestamp time.Time         `json:"timestamp"`
605:     Source    string            `json:"source"`  // identity | policy | reliability | mcp
606:     EventType string            `json:"event_type"`
607:     EntityID  string            `json:"entity_id"`
608:     NodeID    string            `json:"node_id"`
609:     AgentID   string            `json:"agent_id,omitempty"`
610:     Outcome   string            `json:"outcome"` // allow | deny | flag | breach | kill
611:     Detail    map[string]interface{} `json:"detail"`
612:     ChainHash string            `json:"chain_hash"`
613: }
614: 
615: type EventCorrelator struct {
616:     mu     sync.RWMutex
617:     events []*ComplianceEvent
618:     tip    string  // running HMAC-SHA256 chain tip
619:     key    []byte  // HMAC key loaded from root.key
620: }
621: 
622: func (ec *EventCorrelator) Record(source, eventType, entityID, nodeID, agentID, outcome string, detail map[string]interface{})
623: func (ec *EventCorrelator) VerifyChain() error
624: func (ec *EventCorrelator) Query(filter EventFilter) []*ComplianceEvent
625: func (ec *EventCorrelator) Export(format string) ([]byte, error)  // json | csv | ndjson
626: ```
627: 
628: Each governance service receives an `*EventCorrelator` at construction and calls `correlator.Record` on every meaningful state change. The HMAC chain makes each event cryptographically dependent on the previous one — retroactive alteration requires the HMAC key.
629: 
630: The HMAC key is derived from KNIRVSERVER's existing `root.key` secret store.
631: 
632: #### 5-B: Compliance Framework Mapper
633: 
634: **File:** `services/compliance/frameworks.go`
635: 
636: Maps KNIRV governance events to specific control requirements for three frameworks:
637: 
638: ```go
639: type ControlMapping struct {
640:     Framework   string   `json:"framework"`   // GDPR | SOC2 | ISO42001
641:     ControlID   string   `json:"control_id"`  // e.g. "CC6.1"
642:     ControlName string   `json:"control_name"`
643:     EventTypes  []string `json:"event_types"` // which ComplianceEvent.EventType values satisfy this control
644:     Satisfied   bool     `json:"satisfied"`
645:     EvidenceIDs []string `json:"evidence_ids"`

648: type ComplianceReport struct {
649:     GeneratedAt time.Time         `json:"generated_at"`

652:     Framework   string            `json:"framework"`
653:     Controls    []ControlMapping  `json:"controls"`
654:     ChainValid  bool              `json:"chain_valid"`
655:     ReportHash  string            `json:"report_hash"`
656: }
657: 
658: func GenerateReport(framework string, events []*ComplianceEvent, window time.Duration) (*ComplianceReport, error)
659: ```

662: 
663: | Framework | Controls covered |
664: |-----------|-----------------|
665: | GDPR | Art. 22 (automated decision-making), Art. 25 (data minimization), Art. 32 (security of processing) |
666: | SOC 2 | CC6.1 (logical access), CC6.6 (external communication), CC7.2 (monitoring), CC9.2 (vendor risk) |

684: ### Phase 6: Governance Verification CLI
685: 
686: **Location:** `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/`
687: 
688: The project CLI is `knirv` — the Cobra binary in `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/root.go`. There is no separate `knirvctl`. The governance commands are added as a new top-level subcommand following the same pattern as `mcp.go` (which pulls subcommand implementations from `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/mcp/`).
689: 
690: **Files:**
691: 
692: | File | Role |
693: |------|------|
694: | `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance.go` | Declares `governanceCmd`, registers it on `rootCmd` in `init()`, adds subcommand group |
695: | `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance/verify.go` | `VerifyCmd` — verify HMAC chain |
696: | `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance/report.go` | `ReportCmd` — generate compliance report |
697: | `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance/identity.go` | `IdentityCmd` + `IdentityListCmd` — envelope management |
698: | `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance/policy.go` | `PolicyCmd` + `PolicyEvalCmd` — Rego policy evaluation |
699: | `packages/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance/mcp.go` | `MCPCmd` + `MCPAuditCmd` — MCP call audit dump |
700: 
701: **`cmd/governance.go` structure:**
702: 
703: ```go
704: package cmd
705: 
706: import (
707:     "github.com/KNIRV/KNIRV_NETWORK/KNIRVSHELL/cmd/governance"
708:     "github.com/spf13/cobra"
709: )
710: 
711: var governanceCmd = &cobra.Command{
712:     Use:   "governance",
713:     Short: "Inspect and verify KNIRVSERVER governance state",
714:     Long:  `Query trust envelopes, policy decisions, compliance evidence, and MCP audit records from a running KNIRVSERVER instance.`,
715:     Run:   func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) { cmd.Help() },
716: }
717: 
718: func init() {
719:     rootCmd.AddCommand(governanceCmd)
720:     governanceCmd.AddCommand(governance.VerifyCmd)
721:     governanceCmd.AddCommand(governance.ReportCmd)
722:     governanceCmd.AddCommand(governance.IdentityCmd)
723:     governanceCmd.AddCommand(governance.PolicyCmd)
724:     governanceCmd.AddCommand(governance.MCPCmd)
725: }
726: ```
727: 
728: **Conventions (match existing KNIRVSHELL cmd style):**
729: 
730: - Use `github.com/spf13/cobra` for all commands (not `flag`).
731: - Use the package-level `log` (`logrus.New()` from `root.go`) for output — do not create a second logger.
732: - Use `viper.GetString("node_url")` to read `--node-url` from the inherited persistent flag rather than defining a new flag.
733: - HTTP calls go to `viper.GetString("node_url")` (default `http://localhost:8084`). Auth token is read from `~/.knirv.yaml` via viper key `governance.token`.
734: - Use `github.com/spf13/viper` for any command-local config (e.g. `governance.default_framework`).
735: 
736: **Example command surface:**
737: 
738: ```
739: knirv governance verify                   — verify HMAC chain integrity and print summary
740: knirv governance report --framework gdpr  — generate compliance report to stdout
741: knirv governance identity list            — list active trust envelopes
742: knirv governance policy eval --file input.json --policy mypolicy
743: knirv governance mcp audit --limit 50
744: ```

748: ### Phase 7: Framework Interoperability SDK
749: 
750: The SDK is split across two packages matching the existing project split between KNIRVBASE (importable library) and KNIRVSERVER (the running process):
751: 
752: #### 7-A: Client — `packages/KNIRVSDK/go/governance/`
753: 
754: **Module:** `github.com/KNIRV/KNIRV_NETWORK/KNIRVSDK/go` (declared in `packages/KNIRVSDK/go/go.mod`)
755: 
756: **New package path within module:** `github.com/KNIRV/KNIRV_NETWORK/KNIRVSDK/go/governance`
757: 
758: This sits alongside the existing SDK subdirectories — `gateway/`, `transaction/`, `transmission/`, `oracled/` — following the same flat layout. External agent frameworks import this package to embed governance checks without making HTTP calls. It communicates with the `GovernanceAgent` server (Phase 7-B) over a Unix domain socket, keeping the enforcement path sub-millisecond.
759: 
760: No new entries in `packages/KNIRVSDK/go/go.mod` are required — the socket client only needs `net`, `encoding/json`, and `sync` from the standard library.
761: 
762: ```go
763: // packages/KNIRVSDK/go/governance/client.go
764: package governance
765: 
766: // Types are declared locally so KNIRVSDK has no dependency on KNIRVSERVER internals.
767: type TrustEnvelope struct {
768:     IdentityID string     `json:"identity_id"`
769:     NodeID     string     `json:"node_id"`
770:     AgentID    string     `json:"agent_id,omitempty"`
771:     TrustLevel string     `json:"trust_level"`
772:     TrustScore float64    `json:"trust_score"`
773:     ExpiresAt  time.Time  `json:"expires_at"`
774: }
775: 
776: type PolicyInput struct {
777:     NodeID     string                 `json:"node_id"`
778:     AgentID    string                 `json:"agent_id,omitempty"`
779:     Action     string                 `json:"action"`
780:     ActionType string                 `json:"action_type"`
781:     Metrics    map[string]float64     `json:"metrics,omitempty"`
782:     Context    map[string]interface{} `json:"context,omitempty"`
783: }
784: 
785: type PolicyDecision struct {
786:     Decision     string   `json:"decision"`      // allow | deny
787:     Reason       string   `json:"reason,omitempty"`
788:     MatchedRules []string `json:"matched_rules,omitempty"`
789: }
790: 
791: type ToolCallStatus string
792: 
793: const (
794:     ToolCallAllowed  ToolCallStatus = "allowed"
795:     ToolCallDenied   ToolCallStatus = "denied"
796:     ToolCallFlagged  ToolCallStatus = "flagged"
797:     ToolCallBlocked  ToolCallStatus = "blocked"
798: )
799: 
800: // DefaultSocketPath is exported so the KNIRVSERVER GovernanceAgent and this
801: // client agree on the socket location without requiring config on both sides.
802: const DefaultSocketPath = "/var/run/knirvserver/governance.sock"
803: 
804: type Client struct {
805:     socketPath string
806:     conn       net.Conn
807:     mu         sync.Mutex
808: }
809: 
810: func NewClient(socketPath string) (*Client, error)
811: func (c *Client) CheckIdentity(nodeID, agentID string) (*TrustEnvelope, error)
812: func (c *Client) EvaluatePolicy(input PolicyInput) (*PolicyDecision, error)
813: func (c *Client) RecordToolCall(agentID, nodeID, toolName string, args map[string]interface{}) (ToolCallStatus, error)
814: func (c *Client) Close() error
815: ```
816: 
817: The socket protocol — length-prefixed JSON (4-byte big-endian length + JSON body) — is the full wire contract. Any language can implement a compatible client without a generated stub.
818: 
819: #### 7-B: Server — `packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/governance_sdk/`
820: 
821: Runs as a goroutine inside the main KNIRVSERVER process, started during server initialization alongside the other governance services. Uses the same socket path constant (`governance.DefaultSocketPath` or the override from `governance.sdk.socket_path` in `config/governance.yaml`).
822: 
823: ```go
824: // packages/KNIRVSERVER/backend/internal/services/governance_sdk/server.go
825: package governance_sdk
826: 
827: type GovernanceAgent struct {
828:     socketPath string
829:     identity   *identitybridge.IdentityBridge
830:     policy     *policyadapter.PolicyAdapter
831:     mcp        *mcphardening.MCPGateway
832:     listener   net.Listener
833: }
834: 
835: func NewGovernanceAgent(
836:     socketPath string,
837:     ib  *identitybridge.IdentityBridge,
838:     pa  *policyadapter.PolicyAdapter,
839:     mcp *mcphardening.MCPGateway,
840: ) *GovernanceAgent
841: 
842: func (ga *GovernanceAgent) Start() error  // spawns accept loop goroutine
843: func (ga *GovernanceAgent) Stop()
844: ```
845: 
846: `GovernanceAgent` is initialized in `main.go` immediately after the four governance services are constructed (`s.governanceIdentity`, `s.governancePolicy`, `s.governanceMCP`), and `Start()` is called before `ListenAndServe`.

850: ## Sequencing and Dependencies
851: 
852: ```
853: 1-A DID resolver          → 1-B zero-trust middleware (needs envelope validation)
854: 1-C revocation list       → 1-B (needs IsRevoked check)
855: 2-A Rego evaluator        → 2-B per-request enforcement (needs evaluator)
856: 2-B enforcement middleware → 2-C guardrail bridge (needs normalized input)
857: 3-A DVE metric binding    → 3-C SLO definitions (SLO records need real metrics)
858: 3-B escalation pipeline   → 3-C (SLO threshold fires escalation)
859: 4-A argument schema       → 4-B injection detection (scan runs after schema pass)
860: 4-B injection detection   → 4-C response audit (response scanner reuses detector)
861: 5-A event correlator      ← all phases above emit events into it
862: 5-B framework mapper      → 5-C report routes (mapper feeds report generator)
863: 6   CLI                   ← all HTTP routes from 1–5
864: 7   SDK                   ← identity + policy + MCP services (reliability via escalation callback)
865: ```
866: 
867: **Recommended execution order** (each item is independently mergeable):
868: 
869: 1. `1-A` + `1-C` — DID + revocation (no middleware yet, safe to merge standalone)
870: 2. `2-A` — Rego evaluator (additive to `policyadapter`, no behavior change without loaded policies)
871: 3. `4-A` + `4-B` + `4-C` — MCP hardening depth (existing `mcphardening` package, additive)
872: 4. `3-A` + `3-B` + `3-C` — Reliability depth (requires DVEManager interface impl)
873: 5. `1-B` + `2-B` — Middleware (touches request path; needs 1-A and 2-A complete first)
874: 6. `2-C` — GuardrailEngine bridge (requires 2-B working)
875: 7. `5-A` + `5-B` + `5-C` — Compliance layer (depends on all services emitting events)
876: 8. `6` — CLI (depends on all HTTP routes)
877: 9. `7` — SDK (Unix socket server, independent of HTTP routes)

}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) CreateEnvelope(nodeID, agentID string, source IdentitySource, attrs *IdentityAttributes) *TrustEnvelope {
	ib.mu.Lock()
	defer ib.mu.Unlock()

	if attrs == nil {
		attrs = &IdentityAttributes{
			NodeID:      nodeID,
			Environment: "unknown",
		}
	}

	trustScore := ib.calculateTrustScore(attrs)
	trustLevel := ib.scoreToLevel(trustScore)

	env := &TrustEnvelope{
		IdentityID:   uuid.New().String(),
		Source:       source,
		NodeID:       nodeID,
		AgentID:      agentID,
		TrustLevel:   trustLevel,
		TrustScore:   trustScore,
		Metadata:     make(map[string]string),
		Capabilities: make([]string, 0),
		IssuedAt:     time.Now().UTC(),
		ExpiresAt:    time.Now().UTC().Add(ib.defaultTTL),
		Federated:    false,
	}

	ib.envelopes[env.IdentityID] = env
	ib.attributes[env.IdentityID] = attrs
	return env
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) GetEnvelope(identityID string) (*TrustEnvelope, bool) {
	ib.mu.RLock()
	defer ib.mu.RUnlock()
	env, ok := ib.envelopes[identityID]
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	if time.Now().UTC().After(env.ExpiresAt) {
		return nil, false
	}
	return env, true
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) RevokeEnvelope(identityID string) error {
	ib.mu.Lock()
	defer ib.mu.Unlock()
	env, ok := ib.envelopes[identityID]
	if !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("envelope not found: %s", identityID)
	}
	env.ExpiresAt = time.Now().UTC().Add(-1 * time.Hour)
	return nil
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) RefreshEnvelope(identityID string) (*TrustEnvelope, error) {
	ib.mu.Lock()
	defer ib.mu.Unlock()
	env, ok := ib.envelopes[identityID]
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("envelope not found: %s", identityID)
	}
	env.IssuedAt = time.Now().UTC()
	env.ExpiresAt = time.Now().UTC().Add(ib.defaultTTL)
	return env, nil
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) UpdateTrustScore(identityID string, delta float64) (*TrustEnvelope, error) {
	ib.mu.Lock()
	defer ib.mu.Unlock()
	env, ok := ib.envelopes[identityID]
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("envelope not found: %s", identityID)
	}
	newScore := env.TrustScore + delta
	if newScore < 0 {
		newScore = 0
	}
	if newScore > 1.0 {
		newScore = 1.0
	}
	env.TrustScore = newScore
	env.TrustLevel = ib.scoreToLevel(newScore)
	env.IssuedAt = time.Now().UTC()
	return env, nil
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) CreateMapping(internalID, externalID, externalSource, mappingType string, metadata map[string]string) *TrustMapping {
	ib.mu.Lock()
	defer ib.mu.Unlock()

	mapping := &TrustMapping{
		InternalID:      internalID,
		ExternalID:      externalID,
		ExternalSource:  externalSource,
		MappingType:     mappingType,
		MappedAt:        time.Now().UTC(),
		LastVerifiedAt:  time.Now().UTC(),
		MappingMetadata: metadata,
	}

	mappingKey := ib.mappingKey(internalID, externalSource)
	ib.mappings[mappingKey] = mapping
	return mapping
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) GetMapping(internalID, externalSource string) (*TrustMapping, bool) {
	ib.mu.RLock()
	defer ib.mu.RUnlock()
	mapping, ok := ib.mappings[ib.mappingKey(internalID, externalSource)]
	return mapping, ok
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) ListMappings(internalID string) []*TrustMapping {
	ib.mu.RLock()
	defer ib.mu.RUnlock()
	var result []*TrustMapping
	for _, m := range ib.mappings {
		if m.InternalID == internalID {
			result = append(result, m)
		}
	}
	return result
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) ListEnvelopes(nodeID string) []*TrustEnvelope {
	ib.mu.RLock()
	defer ib.mu.RUnlock()
	var result []*TrustEnvelope
	for _, env := range ib.envelopes {
		if nodeID == "" || env.NodeID == nodeID {
			if time.Now().UTC().Before(env.ExpiresAt) {
				result = append(result, env)
			}
		}
	}
	return result
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) UpdateAttributes(identityID string, attrs *IdentityAttributes) error {
	ib.mu.Lock()
	defer ib.mu.Unlock()
	if _, ok := ib.envelopes[identityID]; !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("envelope not found: %s", identityID)
	}
	ib.attributes[identityID] = attrs

	env := ib.envelopes[identityID]
	newScore := ib.calculateTrustScore(attrs)
	env.TrustScore = newScore
	env.TrustLevel = ib.scoreToLevel(newScore)
	env.IssuedAt = time.Now().UTC()
	return nil
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) GetAttributes(identityID string) (*IdentityAttributes, bool) {
	ib.mu.RLock()
	defer ib.mu.RUnlock()
	attrs, ok := ib.attributes[identityID]
	return attrs, ok
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) calculateTrustScore(attrs *IdentityAttributes) float64 {
	if attrs == nil {
		return 0.0
	}
	score := 0.5

	if attrs.Stake > 0 {
		score += 0.15
		if attrs.Stake > 1000 {
			score += 0.1
		}
	}

	if attrs.Reputation > 0 {
		score += attrs.Reputation * 0.2
	}

	if attrs.TEEType != "" {
		score += 0.1
	}

	if attrs.Environment == "production" {
		score += 0.05
	}

	if len(attrs.Roles) > 0 {
		score += 0.05
	}

	if score > 1.0 {
		score = 1.0
	}
	return score
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) scoreToLevel(score float64) TrustLevel {
	switch {
	case score >= 0.9:
		return TrustLevelMaximum
	case score >= 0.7:
		return TrustLevelHigh
	case score >= 0.4:
		return TrustLevelMedium
	case score >= 0.1:
		return TrustLevelLow
	default:
		return TrustLevelNone
	}
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) mappingKey(internalID, externalSource string) string {
	return internalID + ":" + externalSource
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) FederateIdentity(identityID, federationID string) error {
	ib.mu.Lock()
	defer ib.mu.Unlock()
	env, ok := ib.envelopes[identityID]
	if !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("envelope not found: %s", identityID)
	}
	env.Federated = true
	env.FederationID = federationID
	return nil
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) GetStatistics() map[string]interface{} {
	ib.mu.RLock()
	defer ib.mu.RUnlock()
	activeCount := 0
	for _, env := range ib.envelopes {
		if time.Now().UTC().Before(env.ExpiresAt) {
			activeCount++
		}
	}
	return map[string]interface{}{
		"total_envelopes":   len(ib.envelopes),
		"active_envelopes":  activeCount,
		"total_mappings":    len(ib.mappings),
		"trust_distribution": ib.computeTrustDistribution(),
	}
}

func (ib *IdentityBridge) computeTrustDistribution() map[TrustLevel]int {
	dist := map[TrustLevel]int{}
	for _, env := range ib.envelopes {
		if time.Now().UTC().Before(env.ExpiresAt) {
			dist[env.TrustLevel]++
		}
	}
	return dist
}

	ContextFields  []string            `json:"context_fields"`

type PolicyAdapter struct {

	inputs        map[string]*NormalizedPolicyInput
	enforcements  map[string]*NormalizedEnforcement
	contract      PortabilityContract
}

func NewPolicyAdapter() *PolicyAdapter {
	return &PolicyAdapter{
		inputs:       make(map[string]*NormalizedPolicyInput),
		enforcements: make(map[string]*NormalizedEnforcement),
		contract: PortabilityContract{
			Version: "1.0.0",

			MetricNames: []string{
				"cpu_usage", "memory_usage", "network_bandwidth",

				"latency_p50", "latency_p99", "request_count",
			},
			ActionTypes: []string{
				"execute_tool", "read_file", "write_file",
				"network_request", "spawn_agent", "access_memory",
				"invoke_llm", "deploy_plugin",
			},
			ContextFields: []string{
				"environment", "node_type", "agent_role",
				"session_id", "request_id", "user_id",
			},
			OutputFormat: "application/json",
		},
	}
}

	pa.mu.RLock()
	defer pa.mu.RUnlock()
	return pa.contract
}

func (pa *PolicyAdapter) NormalizeInput(nodeID, action, actionType string, metrics map[string]float64, context map[string]interface{}) *NormalizedPolicyInput {
	pa.mu.Lock()
	defer pa.mu.Unlock()

	input := &NormalizedPolicyInput{
		NodeID:     nodeID,
		Action:     action,
		ActionType: actionType,
		Timestamp:  time.Now().UTC(),
		Metrics:    metrics,
		Context:    context,

	pa.inputs[pa.inputKey(nodeID, action)] = input
	return input

func (rc *ReliabilityController) GetOrCreateBreaker(breakerID string) *CircuitBreaker {
	rc.mu.Lock()
	defer rc.mu.Unlock()
	cb, ok := rc.breakers[breakerID]
	if !ok {
		cb = &CircuitBreaker{
			State:           CircuitStateClosed,
			Threshold:       rc.defaultBreakerConfig.Threshold,
			HalfOpenMax:     rc.defaultBreakerConfig.HalfOpenMax,
			RecoveryTimeout: rc.defaultBreakerConfig.RecoveryTimeout,
			LastStateChange: time.Now(),
		}
		rc.breakers[breakerID] = cb
	}
	return cb
}

func (rc *ReliabilityController) transitionToHalfOpenIfExpired(cb *CircuitBreaker) {
	if cb.State == CircuitStateOpen && time.Since(cb.OpenedAt) >= cb.RecoveryTimeout {
		cb.State = CircuitStateHalfOpen
		cb.SuccessCount = 0
		cb.FailureCount = 0
		cb.LastStateChange = time.Now()
	}
}

func (rc *ReliabilityController) RecordSuccess(breakerID string) {
	cb := rc.GetOrCreateBreaker(breakerID)
	cb.mu.Lock()
	defer cb.mu.Unlock()

	rc.transitionToHalfOpenIfExpired(cb)

	switch cb.State {
	case CircuitStateClosed:
		cb.SuccessCount++
		cb.FailureCount = 0
	case CircuitStateHalfOpen:
		cb.SuccessCount++
		cb.FailureCount = 0
		if cb.SuccessCount >= cb.HalfOpenMax {
			cb.State = CircuitStateClosed
			cb.LastStateChange = time.Now()
			cb.SuccessCount = 0
		}
	}
}

func (rc *ReliabilityController) RecordFailure(breakerID string) {
	cb := rc.GetOrCreateBreaker(breakerID)
	cb.mu.Lock()
	defer cb.mu.Unlock()

	rc.transitionToHalfOpenIfExpired(cb)

	switch cb.State {
	case CircuitStateClosed:
		cb.FailureCount++
		cb.SuccessCount = 0
		if cb.FailureCount >= cb.Threshold {
			cb.State = CircuitStateOpen
			cb.OpenedAt = time.Now()
			cb.LastStateChange = time.Now()
		}
	case CircuitStateHalfOpen:
		cb.State = CircuitStateOpen
		cb.OpenedAt = time.Now()
		cb.LastStateChange = time.Now()
		cb.FailureCount++
		cb.SuccessCount = 0
	}
}

func (rc *ReliabilityController) IsRequestAllowed(breakerID string) bool {
	cb := rc.GetOrCreateBreaker(breakerID)
	cb.mu.Lock()
	defer cb.mu.Unlock()

	rc.transitionToHalfOpenIfExpired(cb)

	switch cb.State {
	case CircuitStateClosed:
		return true
	case CircuitStateOpen:
		return false
	case CircuitStateHalfOpen:
		return cb.SuccessCount < cb.HalfOpenMax
	default:
		return false
	}
}

	cb := rc.GetOrCreateBreaker(breakerID)
	cb.mu.Lock()
	defer cb.mu.Unlock()

	rc.transitionToHalfOpenIfExpired(cb)
	return cb.State
}

	if !ok {
		b = &ErrorBudget{
			TotalBudget: rc.defaultBudgetConfig.TotalBudget,
			Period:      rc.defaultBudgetConfig.Period,
			PeriodStart: time.Now(),
		}
		rc.budgets[budgetID] = b

func (rc *ReliabilityController) ConsumeBudget(budgetID string) (float64, bool) {
	b := rc.GetOrCreateBudget(budgetID)
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()

	if b.Remaining == 0 && b.Consumed == 0 && b.Errors == 0 {
		b.Remaining = b.TotalBudget
	}

	if time.Since(b.PeriodStart) >= b.Period {
		b.Remaining = b.TotalBudget
		b.Consumed = 0
		b.Errors = 0
		b.TotalRequests = 0
		b.PeriodStart = time.Now()
	}

	b.TotalRequests++

	exhausted := b.Remaining <= 0
	return b.Remaining, !exhausted
}

func (rc *ReliabilityController) RecordBudgetError(budgetID string) {
	b := rc.GetOrCreateBudget(budgetID)
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()

	if b.Remaining == 0 && b.Consumed == 0 && b.Errors == 0 {
		b.Remaining = b.TotalBudget
	}

	b.Errors++
	b.Consumed = float64(b.Errors) / float64(b.TotalRequests)
	if b.TotalRequests == 0 {
		b.TotalRequests = 1
		b.Consumed = 1.0
	}
	b.Remaining = b.TotalBudget - b.Consumed
	if b.Remaining < 0 {
		b.Remaining = 0
	}
}

	}

	policy, ok := rc.escalations[nodeID]
	rc.mu.RUnlock()

	if !ok {
		policy = &rc.defaultEscalation
	}

	switch {
	case value >= policy.ShutdownThreshold:
		return EscalationLevelShutdown
	case value >= policy.CriticalThreshold:

	rc.mu.Lock()
	defer rc.mu.Unlock()

	key := rc.killKey(agentID, nodeID)
	ks, ok := rc.killSwitches[key]
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no kill switch found for agent %s on node %s", agentID, nodeID)

	if ks.State == KillSwitchStateTripped {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("kill switch already tripped for agent %s", agentID)

	ks.State = KillSwitchStateTripped
	ks.Reason = reason
	ks.TrippedBy = trippedBy
	ks.TriggeredAt = time.Now()

	event := &BreachEvent{

		Level:     EscalationLevelShutdown,

func (rc *ReliabilityController) GetStatistics() map[string]interface{} {
	rc.mu.RLock()
	defer rc.mu.RUnlock()

	openBreakers := 0
	totalBreakers := len(rc.breakers)
	for _, cb := range rc.breakers {
		cb.mu.RLock()
		if cb.State == CircuitStateOpen {
			openBreakers++
		}
		cb.mu.RUnlock()
	}

	totalKillSwitches := len(rc.killSwitches)
	tripped := 0
	for _, ks := range rc.killSwitches {
		ks.mu.RLock()
		if ks.State == KillSwitchStateTripped {
			tripped++
		}
		ks.mu.RUnlock()
	}

	unresolvedBreaches := 0
	for _, e := range rc.breachEvents {
		if !e.Resolved {
			unresolvedBreaches++
		}
	}

	return map[string]interface{}{
		"total_circuit_breakers": totalBreakers,
		"open_circuit_breakers":  openBreakers,
		"total_error_budgets":    len(rc.budgets),
		"total_kill_switches":    totalKillSwitches,
		"tripped_kill_switches":  tripped,

		"unresolved_breaches":    unresolvedBreaches,
	}

	return agentID + "@" + nodeID
}

func (rc *ReliabilityController) ListBreakers() map[string]CircuitState {
	rc.mu.RLock()
	defer rc.mu.RUnlock()
	result := make(map[string]CircuitState, len(rc.breakers))
	for id, cb := range rc.breakers {
		cb.mu.RLock()
		state := cb.State
		if state == CircuitStateOpen && time.Since(cb.OpenedAt) >= cb.RecoveryTimeout {
			state = CircuitStateHalfOpen
		}
		result[id] = state
		cb.mu.RUnlock()
	}
	return result
}

func (rc *ReliabilityController) ListKillSwitches() []*KillSwitch {
	rc.mu.RLock()
	defer rc.mu.RUnlock()
	result := make([]*KillSwitch, 0, len(rc.killSwitches))
	for _, ks := range rc.killSwitches {
		result = append(result, ks)
	}
	return result
}

// AuthMiddleware handles authentication and authorization

	authRequired bool

func (am *AuthMiddleware) SetAuthRequired(required bool) {
	am.authRequired = required
}

// UserClaims represents JWT claims for a user
type UserClaims struct {
	UserID   string `json:"user_id"`
	Username string `json:"username"`
	Role     string `json:"role"`
	jwt.RegisteredClaims
}

// AuthContext represents authentication context
type AuthContext struct {
	UserID   string
	Username string
	Role     string
	Token    string
}

// Context keys
type contextKey string

const (
	AuthContextKey contextKey = "auth_context"
)

// NewAuthMiddleware creates a new authentication middleware
func NewAuthMiddleware(db *database.BuntDBManager, jwtSecret string, authRequired bool) (*AuthMiddleware, error) {
	if jwtSecret == "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("JWT secret cannot be empty")
	}

	return &AuthMiddleware{
		db:           db,
		jwtSecret:    []byte(jwtSecret),
		authRequired: authRequired,
	}, nil
}

// GenerateToken generates a JWT token for a user
func (am *AuthMiddleware) GenerateToken(userID, username, role string, duration time.Duration) (string, error) {
	claims := UserClaims{
		UserID:   userID,
		Username: username,
		Role:     role,
		RegisteredClaims: jwt.RegisteredClaims{
			ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now().Add(duration)),
			IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
			NotBefore: jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
			Issuer:    "knirv-server",
			Subject:   userID,
		},
	}

	token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, claims)
	return token.SignedString(am.jwtSecret)
}

// ValidateToken validates a JWT token and returns the claims
func (am *AuthMiddleware) ValidateToken(tokenString string) (*UserClaims, error) {
	token, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(tokenString, &UserClaims{}, func(token *jwt.Token) (interface{}, error) {
		if _, ok := token.Method.(*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC); !ok {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected signing method: %v", token.Header["alg"])
		}
		return am.jwtSecret, nil
	})

	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if claims, ok := token.Claims.(*UserClaims); ok && token.Valid {
		// Check if token is revoked
		if am.isTokenRevoked(tokenString) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("token has been revoked")
		}
		return claims, nil
	}

	return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid token")
}

// RevokeToken revokes a JWT token
func (am *AuthMiddleware) RevokeToken(tokenString string) error {
	// Create a hash of the token for storage
	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(tokenString))
	tokenHash := hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])

	// Store the revoked token hash in the database
	// This is a simplified implementation - in production you'd want to clean up expired tokens
	return am.db.Transaction(func(tx *buntdb.Tx) error {
		// Store with expiration time to allow cleanup
		expirationTime := time.Now().Add(24 * time.Hour) // Adjust based on your token expiration
		revokedToken := map[string]interface{}{
			"token_hash": tokenHash,
			"revoked_at": time.Now(),
			"expires_at": expirationTime,
		}

		data, _ := json.Marshal(revokedToken)
		_, _, err := tx.Set("revoked_tokens:"+tokenHash, string(data), nil)
		return err
	})
}

// isTokenRevoked checks if a token has been revoked
func (am *AuthMiddleware) isTokenRevoked(tokenString string) bool {
	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(tokenString))
	tokenHash := hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])

	var isRevoked bool
	am.db.ViewTransaction(func(tx *buntdb.Tx) error {
		val, err := tx.Get("revoked_tokens:" + tokenHash)
		isRevoked = (err == nil && val != "")
		return nil
	})

// RequireAuth middleware that requires authentication

		// handlers do not fail their own GetAuthContext checks.
		if !am.authRequired {

				UserID:   "anonymous",
				Username: "anonymous",
				Role:     "admin",
			}

				if len(parts) == 2 && parts[0] == "Bearer" {

		if claims, err := am.ValidateToken(tokenString); err == nil {

				Username: claims.Username,
				Role:     claims.Role,

// validateSessionToken checks for a session token in the database
func (am *AuthMiddleware) validateSessionToken(token string) (*AuthContext, error) {
	var authCtx *AuthContext

	err := am.db.ViewTransaction(func(tx *buntdb.Tx) error {
		// Check user sessions
		found := false
		tx.AscendKeys("sessions:*", func(key, value string) bool {
			var s struct {
				UserID   string    `json:"user_id"`
				Token    string    `json:"token"`
				IsActive bool      `json:"is_active"`
				ExpiresAt time.Time `json:"expires_at"`
			}
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(value), &s); err == nil && s.Token == token && s.IsActive && time.Now().Before(s.ExpiresAt) {
				authCtx = &AuthContext{
					UserID: s.UserID,
					Token:  token,
					Role:   "user", // Default for session
				}
				found = true
				return false
			}
			return true
		})

		if found {
			return nil
		}

		// Check DVE rentals (access tokens)
		tx.AscendKeys("rental:*", func(key, value string) bool {
			var r struct {
				UserID      string    `json:"user_id"`
				AccessToken string    `json:"access_token"`
				Status      string    `json:"status"`
				EndTime     time.Time `json:"end_time"`
			}
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(value), &r); err == nil && r.AccessToken == token && r.Status == "active" && time.Now().Before(r.EndTime) {
				authCtx = &AuthContext{
					UserID: r.UserID,
					Token:  token,
					Role:   "validator", // DVE tokens act as validator role
				}
				found = true
				return false
			}
			return true
		})

		if found {
			return nil
		}

		return fmt.Errorf("session token not found")
	})

	return authCtx, err
}

			if len(parts) == 2 && parts[0] == "Bearer" {

package middleware

import (
